This Crl.P Is Filed Under Section 482 Of The Code Of
Criminal Procedure, 1973 Praying To Quash The Criminal
Proceedings Being Registered In Fir No.123/2020 For The
Offence Punishable Under Sections 406, 420 Of Ipc In The
Davanagere South Circle, Davanagere Police Station,
Pending On The File Of J.M.F.C. - I Court, Davanagere, In So
Far As The Petitioner (Accused No.2) Is Concerned.
 This Petition, Coming On For Admission, This Day, The
Court Made The Following:
 Order

The petitioner being accused No.2 has challenged the investigation launched against him in Crime No.123/2020 for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420 of IPC pending consideration before the Judicial Magistrate First Class - I, Davanagere (henceforth referred to as 'Trial Court').
2.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class - I, Davanagere
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 informed respondent No.1 on 12.10.2020 that the petitioner and his wife approached it for a loan of Rs.75,00,000/- to establish a photo studio.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.75,00,000/- was sanctioned and released to them.
Though the wife of the petitioner had paid installments upto 10.07.2019, she did not pay the balance installments.

Thereafter, when they visited the photo studio, they found that all the valuable equipments in the photo studio NC:
2023:KHC:40943 were missing, while interior decoration was being removed.
Then the respondent No.2 contacted the petitioner and his wife and informed them that all the equipments should be made available for inspection.
Accordingly, on 29.07.2019, the officials of respondent No.2 visited the photo studio and found that several equipments were not available in the studio.
It alleged that the wife of the petitioner was unable to give satisfactory reply about the other equipments.
Consequent to which, the respondent No.2 lodged a complaint before the Deputy Commissioner on 28.08.2019 requesting him to help in securing the missing articles.

The respondent No.2 claimed that on 19.09.2019, a search was conducted in the photo studio and the equipments available in the premises were seized on 04.12.2019 and were valued at a sum of Rs.19,79,000/.

The respondent No.2 therefore, alleged that the petitioner and his wife had jointly attempted to defraud the respondent No.2.
3.

Based on this, respondent No.1 registered Crime No.123/2020 for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420 of IPC and took up investigation, which is challenged in this petition.
NC: 2023:KHC:40943 4.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner was only a guarantor for the loan raised by the accused No.1 (wife of the petitioner) and therefore, no criminality could be Suresh P vs The State on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4972269/
2 attributed to the petitioner.
He submitted that the respondent No.2 has initiated other proceedings under the State Financial Corporation Act and therefore, the instant prosecution is unwarranted.

He also submits that the petitioner and his wife are not on good terms and that the suit in O.S.No.308/2019 was filed before the Principal Civil Judge, Davanagere, for perpetual injunction restraining the accused No.1 and others from removing the articles from the premises and that the Court had granted an order of injunction from withdrawing or transferring any money from the bank accounts.
He therefore, submits that the petitioner is innocent of the allegations alleged against him.
He also submits that the accused No.1 herself had submitted a letter before the respondent No.2 owning up her mistakes and also that she was unable to pay installments in time.
He therefore, contends that the petitioner is innocent of the allegations and consequently, the investigation launched against him deserves to be halted.

The learned counsel has relied upon the following decisions:-
NC: 2023:KHC:40943 1. Hridaya Ranjan Prasad Verma and others vs. State of Bihar [(2000) 4 SCC 168].
2. Randheer Singh vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and others [(2021) 14 SCC 626]
3. Mitesh Kumar J Sha vs. State of Karnataka and others [(2022) 14 SCC 572]
4. Vilas Deore vs. State of Karnataka [Crl.P.No.4346/2022]

sentences.text: 5. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 on the other hand submits that the fact that the petitioner and the accused No.1 had constituted a partnership firm after receiving loan of Rs.75,00,000/- from the respondent No.2 is not disputed.
He submits that the petitioner was not unaware of the activities undertaken in the photo studio and also about the missing equipments from the photo studio.

He therefore,
submits that the question whether the petitioner was innocent of the accusation against him or not has to be established after investigation and this Court cannot prejudge the issue.
6. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
The loan application form filed by the wife of the petitioner/accused No.1 discloses that the petitioner had guaranteed the repayment of the loan raised by the accused No.1.
It is also not in dispute that the petitioner and his wife after receiving the loan, had constituted a partnership firm to pursue the business in photography.

The fact that the loan was utilized for the purpose of purchasing equipments is evident from the complaint itself where the respondent No.2 claims that the loan was utilized for the purpose of purchasing equipments required for the photography business.

The fact that on an inspection of the premises, equipments worth Rs.19,00,000/- were Suresh P vs The State on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4972269/
3 only available, while all other equipments were missing, gives an impression that the petitioner and his wife had moved out many equipments for some reasons.

It is for the investigating officer to verify whether this movement of articles was due to any genuine reason or whether the equipments were taken away by the petitioner and his wife for other purpose.
In that view of the matter, this Court cannot prejudge the issue and hold that the petitioner was innocence of the allegations alleged against him.
The decisions relied upon by the learned counsel for the petitioner are primarily in respect of an offence between an agreement holder and a purchaser.
The Courts have held from time to time that when the parties are governed by a contract, the question of invoking provisions of Section 415 or 420 of IPC does not arise.
In that view of the matter, the judgments relied upon by the learned counsel for the petitioner would not help him in any manner.
Consequently, this petition lacks merit and is dismissed.
